summary: Intermittent 401s in private deployment when IdP provides duplicate eduPersonPrincipalName entries causing tenant routing ambiguity
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FluxBank) reports intermittent 401 Unauthorized responses when users log in to their private VPC deployment via IdP (SAML, IdP-initiated). The problem surfaced after an IdP change to include both eduPersonPrincipalName (eppn) and mail attributes; sometimes the request is routed to the correct tenant, other times it resolves to a different org alias and returns 401.

Impact:
- Multiple end users across FluxBank experience failed logins (~5-15% of login attempts).
- Affects production in us-east region for the private deployment; blocks admin operations for impacted users.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane, v2.9.1)
- Ingress: NGINX edge-proxy (customer-managed)
- Identity proxy: redwood-identity-proxy v1.12.0
- IdP: On-prem SAML Identity Provider (vendor: OneAuth) configured for IdP-initiated SSO, signed & encrypted assertions

Timeline / Recent changes:
- 2026-02-25: FluxBank updated IdP mapping to include mail + eppn for compatibility with new downstream systems.
- 2026-02-26: First support reports of intermittent 401s.
- 2026-02-27: Ticket opened by Support.

Observed behavior:
- SAML assertion contains both an eppn attribute and an email attribute; eppn is duplicated (e.g., "alice@example.com" appears twice in eppn array).
- When identity-proxy header selection picks the first attribute value the tenant resolves correctly; when it picks the second (or a different attribute order after LB reordering) tenant lookup fails resulting in 401.
- Failures correlate with certain upstream load-balancer nodes and client IP ranges.

Expected behavior:
- Identity proxy should deterministically canonicalize the identity attribute used for tenant resolution (prefer single-valued eppn, fall back to mail only if eppn absent) and not be sensitive to attribute ordering in SAML assertion or header reordering at the edge.

Workaround (temporary):
- Customer reverted to previous IdP mapping that provided a single eppn attribute per assertion; this reduced failure rate but is not acceptable long-term for their new integrations.

Notes: please see attached saml-response debug blob and header dump for a failing vs a succeeding authentication attempt.
steps_to_reproduce: Configure private deployment with customer IdP (IdP-initiated SAML).
Update IdP attribute mapping so SAML assertion includes both eppn (multi-valued) and mail attributes.
Send repeated IdP-initiated SAML logins from multiple client IPs behind the customer's LB.
Observe that ~5-15% of attempts return 401 while others succeed; compare header ordering and identity-proxy logs between success/failure attempts.
logs: 2026-02-26T14:12:03Z identity-proxy INFO Received SAML response for RelayState=... status=Success
identity-proxy DEBUG extracted attributes: { eppn: ["alice@example.com", "alice@example.com"], mail: ["alice@example.com"] }
ingress nginx: upstream header reorder detected; X-User-EPPN header present, values:\"alice@example.com, alice@example.com\"
auth ERROR tenant-resolver: no tenant matched for identifier 'alice@example.com' (attempted aliases: flux-ops, flux-bank) -> 401
comments: 2026-02-27 09:03 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Reproduced using a local SAML response capture. Escalating to Identity team. Added Jordan for routing investigation.
2026-02-27 11:41 - Customer (FluxBank - Ravi Menon): After reverting the mapping failures dropped but we need both attributes for downstreams. Please advise a long-term fix.

2026-02-28 10:15 - Identity (Jordan Kim): Found that identity-proxy accepts comma-separated header values from ingress and naively splits into array preserving ordering. We're seeing duplicated eppn values in the array and tenant lookup uses array[0] without canonicalization.

2026-02-28 16:22 - SRE (Maya Lopez): Correlated failures to two LB nodes performing header folding; created INT-45021 to track ingress config change. Will route traffic away from those nodes as mitigation.

2026-03-01 08:08 - Support (Aisha Patel): Temporary mitigation applied by customer (revert mapping). Identity team drafting a code change to normalize and dedupe eppn and prefer configured tenant claim. PR linked in investigation notes.
investigation_notes: Identity-proxy behavior: tenant resolution currently uses first element of identity attribute array without dedupe/canonicalization. Edge/proxy may change attribute ordering when serializing headers.
Ingress folding: two customer LB nodes concatenate multiple SAML-to-header attributes into a single header string. This results in duplicated values and ordering differences between nodes.
Hypothesis: when header ordering yields an alias that maps to a different tenant namespace we observe 401. The IdP duplicate eppn introduced non-determinism.

Reproduction: captured two SAML responses from FluxBank; identical assertion payloads resulted in different header orderings after the ingress. Identity-proxy accepted both and resolved tenant differently.

Mitigation options evaluated: (1) enforce single-valued attribute on IdP side (customer reverted), (2) normalize/dedupe in identity-proxy before tenant lookup, (3) add explicit tenant claim mapping in config to avoid relying on attribute ordering.
resolution: In Progress - short-term: customer reverted IdP mapping to single-valued eppn. Long-term: engineering to implement normalization and deterministic selection in identity-proxy (dedupe + prefer configured tenant claim). Patch PR opened and linked; awaiting review and canary deployment in staging before rolling to private control planes.
